fatal_errors: Replaces the target single-crystal equiatomic FeNiCrMn FCC model with an as-cast or wrought CoCrFeMnNi polycrystalline material.
Posits an FCC/BCC mixed-phase mediator even though the target behavior arises from Shockley partial dislocations and stacking faults without BCC transformation.
Introduces twinning and grain-boundary sliding, whereas the target reports no twinning and a periodic single crystal without grain boundaries.
Uses quasi-static experimental strain rates rather than the molecular-dynamics range of 10^8-10^10 s^-1.
Omits crystallographic loading orientation, temperature-dependent yield softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, and rate-dependent dislocation density.
Provides arbitrary numerical strength and ductility improvements with no cited evidence or derivation.
explanation: The response only aligns at the broad level of proposing a deformation mechanism for an HEA. It does not reconstruct the material state, loading protocol, conditions, mediator, mechanism, or observed trends of the target. Its baseline changes both composition and phase constitution, so any comparison would confound the proposed effect. In-situ TEM could in principle distinguish some deformation modes, but the design does not isolate FCC/BCC heterogeneity from composition, grain structure, or processing, and first-principles calculations are not an adequate direct simulation of the proposed grain-boundary and dynamic mechanisms. The falsification thresholds are unsupported and test performance rather than the claimed causal mechanism. With no prior evidence supplied—and with central claims conflicting with the target—the hypothesis is unsupported rather than a partial reconstruction.
